clue.text: Casual worker turned up first

indicators.note: placed up first means this piece goes at the front, ahead of the worker

parts.note: milk that has turned has gone off
a hand is a manual worker, as in a farm hand

explanation.surface: A labourer showed up early for a shift, doing no more than casual work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' is the sense of milk gone sour; 'up first' says that piece leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a casual, unconcerned manner is an offhand one.

clue.text: Comment made about blunder, so changed around procedure

indicators.note: around means the scrambled pair wraps about the procedure piece
changed tells us the two letters of so are swapped into a new order

parts.note: OP is short for operation, a medical procedure

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a mistake and then switches round how things are done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' swaps the two letters of 'so' to OS, which goes 'around' the procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation people utter on making a slip or small mistake.

clue.text: Officer's in leading truck with new soldier, eating pork pie

indicators.note: eating loosely signals the pork pie piece being taken up alongside the rest

parts.note: the leading runner is in first place
pork pie is rhyming slang for lie
a ute is a utility truck, an Australian pickup
a soldier ant, so ant stands for soldier

explanation.surface: An officer rides in the front truck with a new recruit who is snacking on a pork pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' only loosely joins LIE to its neighbours: the pieces run in order. Pork pie = LIE is Cockney rhyming slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank of junior commissioned officer, especially in the navy, so an officer; the 's stands for is.

clue.text: Deeply aroused by a fine, exotic material

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
lamé is a fabric woven with metallic threads, an exotic material

explanation.surface: Someone stirred to passion by a fine and exotic fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: burning with passion or excitement, as in hearts on fire.

clue.text: Do I, within three days, start to lack energy?

indicators.note: within says the single letter I goes inside the run of three days

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day, so three of them gives DDD

indicators.note: start to means just the opening letter of lack is used

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A question about whether three days of something will leave one drained of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is the definition in its slang sense of swindle, not the verb of action.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: to do someone is to cheat or swindle them.

clue.text: What's central to Moscow and Stalin's shameful episode?

indicators.note: central to means only the middles of the two names survive, the outer pairs of each name going, while the short joining word stays whole

explanation.surface: A question about what lay at the heart of Moscow and of Stalin's disgraceful history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central to' covers both names: Moscow keeps SC and Stalin keeps AL, with AND left whole between them; the outer pairs MO, OW, ST, IN are what goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a disgraceful event that causes public outrage.

clue.text: A vehicle used by groundsman, ultimately, has pulled up outside grassy area

indicators.note: outside means the reversed piece goes around the rest
pulled up in a down clue means the word has is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of groundsman

explanation.surface: A groundsman's van has been pulled up on the edge of a grassy area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' turns HAS into SAH, which goes 'outside' A, VAN and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a savannah is open grassland, typically in tropical regions.

clue.text: Publicity material was dishonest, containing empty blurb made up on the spot

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is publicity material

indicators.note: containing means the dishonest verb holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: lied means was dishonest

indicators.note: empty means blurb loses its insides, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: An advertisement told lies, its empty blurb improvised on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' strips blurb to its outer letters; 'containing' puts those inside the dishonest verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: improvised speech or performance, said without preparation.

clue.text: Body of foreign officials decline to see racist MP when travelling around county

parts.note: a dip is a decline, as in a dip in sales
lo is an old word meaning see or behold

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters wrap the county abbreviation
when travelling means the letters of racist MP move about into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to refuse to meet a bigoted MP who is touring a county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when travelling' rearranges RACIST MP into MATICRPS, placed 'around' CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the collective of ambassadors and envoys posted to a country's capital.

clue.text: Lothario really liked to play with fire, ultimately getting knocked out

indicators.note: to play with means the letters of really liked are toyed with and rearranged
getting knocked out means the letter from fire is dropped from the shuffled pool
ultimately means the final letter of fire

explanation.surface: A seducer who really liked playing with fire ends up knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E (end of 'fire', 'getting knocked out') from REALLY LIKED and rearrange ('to play with') the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a Lothario is a womaniser, after the seducer in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent.

clue.text: Menace from political extremists maintaining anger towards the West

indicators.note: maintaining means the outer pair holds the reversed piece between them
the extremists of political are its outermost letters
towards the West in an across clue means the word is written leftwards, backwards

parts.note: ire means anger

explanation.surface: A threat posed by political radicals who keep up hostility to Western nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'towards the West' reads anger's synonym leftwards; 'maintaining' holds it inside political's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: danger or threat, as in to be in peril or under menace.

clue.text: Worked on document to guard against European backsliding

indicators.note: to guard means the document wraps around the reversed piece

parts.note: a deed is a legal document

indicators.note: backsliding means the European and against pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a Pole is a European, from Poland
V, for versus, means against

explanation.surface: Someone drafts a document to protect against a European relapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backsliding' reverses POLE plus V to VELOP; DEED surrounds it ('to guard').
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have worked on an idea or a plan is to have built it up or elaborated it.

clue.text: Impediment must be beginning to upset Lancashire's opener, batting with good defensive action

indicators.note: to upset means the letters of must with that letter are knocked into a new order
beginning means the opening letter of be

parts.note: the opener of Lancashire is its first letter, with a nod to a cricket opening batsman
a side batting in cricket is in
in cricket a block is a defensive stroke that stops the ball

explanation.surface: A cricket report: something has upset Lancashire's opening batsman, who keeps blocking defensively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to upset' rearranges MUST + B into STUMB. Cricket terms: the opener is the first batsman; a block is a dead-bat defensive shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an obstacle that hinders progress.

clue.text: When introducing frontrunners in election, Labour instils egalitarianism but I refuse to be taken in by it

definitions.text: refuse to be taken in by it

indicators.note: introducing means the word When takes the run of initials inside it
frontrunners in means the initial letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A political grumble: Labour preaches equality at election time, but the speaker won't be fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' is rubbish, not the verb; 'taken in' is literal, not deceived.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a wheeled household rubbish container, into which waste is put.

clue.text: Being ahead of Independent and Republican, finally triumph by a narrow margin

indicators.note: by means set beside, so the a follows on next
being ahead of means placed in front of the following letters
finally means the last letter of triumph

explanation.surface: An election result: leading the Independent and Republican candidates, someone finally wins by a whisker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by a narrow margin' looks like one phrase, but 'a' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to win by a whisker is to win by the smallest possible margin.

clue.text: Degree by which Coe leads the entire field in sport

indicators.note: leads means this name goes in front of the following piece

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree
Seb Coe is the British Olympic middle-distance runner
the entire field is all of the runners

explanation.surface: An athletics scene: Coe is clear of the whole field.
explanation.walkthrough: Sebastian (Seb) Coe is a British Olympic champion at 1500 metres.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bat-and-ball game, the American national pastime.

clue.text: Exquisite crackers — three each left

indicators.note: crackers means mad, so the letters of three go wild

explanation.surface: Three fancy Christmas crackers are left for each person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' rearranges THREE into ETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: delicate and light, almost too refined for this world.

clue.text: Photograph's not large — gosh, it needs blowing up!

indicators.note: needs blowing up means the letters are blasted apart and reassembled

parts.note: the word not kept as written, with L, the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A photo that isn't big enough needs enlarging, says someone with a 'gosh'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing up' looks like enlarging the photo, but it is the signal to rearrange; 'not large' reads as a description yet supplies NOT plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or camera term: a shot taken from far away, showing a wide scene.

clue.text: Old antique needing restoration is something that could be done by summer?

definitions.text: something that could be done by summer?

indicators.note: needing restoration means these letters must be put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: An old antique needs restoring, maybe by next summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is one who does sums, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a mathematical statement of equality is the sort of thing someone who sums works out.

clue.text: Four iron used to secure par, say?

indicators.note: used to secure means the iron symbol holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A golfer takes a four iron to make par.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four iron' looks like one golf club but splits into a Roman numeral and a chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: par for a long golf hole may be this number of strokes, hence the 'say'.

clue.text: Supporter meets goal hero

indicators.note: meets means the two pieces join side by side

parts.note: a leg supports a table or a body
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A fan meets a goal-scoring hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a celebrated figure, as in a sporting great.

clue.text: In which, ultimately, a cat seizes mouse's tail

indicators.note: seizes means the cat piece grabs the letter and holds it inside

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of which
tail means the last letter of mouse

explanation.surface: A scene where a cat catches a mouse by its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: TOM takes H inside ('seizes'): T-H-OM. 'In' is the definition, as in being at home rather than out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who is in is present in their own house, not out.

clue.text: One drifting at sea allowed a day to consume cold food item

parts.note: an iceberg is a mass of ice floating at sea
let means allowed

indicators.note: to consume means the day abbreviation swallows the cold letter

parts.note: Tue is short for Tuesday, a day
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone adrift at sea was given a day's ration of cold food.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a crisp, round variety of salad leaf, an item of food.

clue.text: Selfish person getting a lift — carry on without me

indicators.note: getting a lift in a down clue means the letters are raised up, so read backwards
without means the letters of me are taken away

parts.note: resume means carry on

explanation.surface: A selfish hitchhiker tells others to carry on without them.
explanation.walkthrough: RESUME 'without' ME leaves RESU, which 'getting a lift' turns over.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who exploits others for their own ends.

clue.text: Vehicle's slower? Sounds like damage to pump, possibly

indicators.note: sounds like means a phrase spoken aloud gives the answer

parts.note: to break a shoe, a pump being a light shoe, damages it

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a slow vehicle, possibly from pump damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pump' is a plimsoll or dancing shoe, not a fuel or water pump.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a curved block pressed against a wheel to slow a vehicle.

clue.text: Minor manufacturer not opening plant

indicators.note: not opening means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Morris built the Morris Minor, a classic British car

explanation.surface: A small-scale maker fails to open a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor' is a car, the Morris Minor, a classic small British car; 'plant' is a flower, not a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an iris whose root yields a fragrant powder.

clue.text: Phone school back, leaving message

indicators.note: back means these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Tel is short for telephone
Eton is the English public school

explanation.surface: Someone rings their school back after leaving it a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses TEL + ETON. Eton is a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small folded card used for writing a short note.

clue.text: Theatre assistant's right to invest in short course

indicators.note: to invest in means the right letter is placed inside the trimmed course
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: dessert is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: A stagehand tries to put their money into a short course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims DESSERT to DESSER; R goes inside it ('to invest in'). The 's in 'assistant's' means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a theatre worker who helps actors into their costumes.
